page.layout: One page of text, with two medallion engravings at the top (not text). Running head centred at top. Page number at top right. Two paragraphs of main text in one column, with a short signature mark at the foot right. No margin notes, no catchword.

main_text.l: IVSTINIANVS huius nominis secundus, qui etiā Iu-
stinus quartus dicitur, Heraclianæ stirpis vltimus, imperat post
patrem anno mundi 4648. à Christo nato 686. hunc pater Con-
stantinus 4. imperij hæredē reliquerat, & fratribus minoribus,
ne ad imperium aspirarent, nares absciderat. Praui hic ingenij,
synodum aduersus sextam à patre celebratā indixit: aduersan-
tem Papam cōprehendi iussit, quòd hanc synodū minimè pro-
barer. Bellum in Arabas & Bulgaros cōtra fœdus mouit, vtrun-
que infeliciter gessit. Ammirathus Saracenorū Rex cum eo fœ-
dus icit, Africámque restituit. Tum crudelitate in suos inuisior
factus, imperio deturbatur anno imperij 10. & relegatur Cher-
sonā, nare prius abscissa: opera Bulgarorum post annos sex re-
stitutus in hostes sæuit: Tiberiū qui Leoncio successerat, fugat:
Callinicum exoculat: ac quoties truncas nares mungit, vnū ali-
quem ex iis qui Leontio fauerāt trucidat. Post annos sex resti-
tutionis, Chersonā euertere studens, à Philippico, quem exilio
dānauerat cum Tiberio filio, bello superatur, & occiditur. Egn.
lib. 2. Pau. Diac. lib. 8. Ab. Vrsper.
LEONTIVS, qui & Leo secundus, adnitente Callinico
Patriarcha Constātinopolitano, Iustinianum imperium detur-
bat, imperiúmque inuadit, anno mundi 4658. à Christo nato
696. itaque ab Heraclio, qui Phocā occidit, in vna gente impe-
ratum est annis plus 80. quod vix vlli priorum contigit: fuit Iu-
stinianus sextus continua serie ab Heraclio Imperator, tradi-
tūmque est imperium velut per manus Heraclianæ stirpi, quæ
defecit in hoc Iustiniano. Porrò Leontius itidem cum infecta
re ab expeditione Africana rediret imperio pellitur à Tiberio
Absimaro, post annos tres, nasóque mutilatur, & in carcerem
truditur. Egna. lib. 2. Diac. lib. 8.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions at the top: left "IMP. IVSTINIANVS II AVG." (bearded bust, laureate, facing right); right "IMP. LEONTI..." with "...S P F AVG" legend (bust in crown, facing right). Not transcribed as text beyond the legends. The LEONTIVS heading is a paragraph opener in larger capitals, so it was set as a level-1 head only if treated as a section title; it is printed mid-text as a paragraph opener. Marks: "Hhh 2" is a gathering signature. Possible [?] readings: none marked with certainty; the coin legends are partly abraded.
